options.text: Stage 0 hosts the input embedding and Stage $p-1$ hosts the output head. Because they reside on different physical GPUs, their gradients must be synchronized via an explicit cross-stage All-Reduce before the optimizer step.
The number of micro-batches m is smaller than the pipeline depth p, so some stages sit idle for an entire iteration.
The 1F1B schedule interleaves forward and backward passes in the wrong order, so a stage computes a backward pass before its matching forward pass has produced an activation.
Activation checkpointing is enabled on every stage except the last, so the last stage's peak memory is far higher than the others'.

explanation: Diagnostic Analysis: Stage 0 hosts the input embedding and Stage $p-1$ hosts the output head. Because they reside on different physical GPUs, their gradients must be synchronized via an explicit cross-stage All-Reduce before the optimizer step.
